Quietly slipping under the lily pad covered surface, water slides of its slick, dark red carapace as the wrakis stealthy approaches its prey. 
A long fluted extension of its abdomen continues taking in oxygen as it waits unmoving for a moment to strike. When a large murrow 
swims by unaware, scythe-like forelimbs slash out to grip the large fi sh as it plunges its proboscis deep into the scaled body, unleashing 
a torrent of digestive fluids to quickly dissolve the unfortunate fi sh’s interior into a fleshy pulp. At six feet long, the large insect is far 
from the apex predator within any given region, but with its ability to hunt anywhere from the dark confi nes of the Umbrawells to 
beneath the roots of the Wealdwoods, to the coastal Strands, this arthropod can be found waiting to strike from any dark crevice.
Class - Insecta • Genus Derived Evolution - Curicta • Niche - Generalist Carnivore

Multiattack Th e wrakis makes two attacks, it can use its Chitin 
Fore Blades or Needling Proboscis in any combination.
Chitin Fore Blades Melee Attack Roll: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one

target has the Grappled condition.
Needling Proboscis Constitution Saving Th row: DC 14, one creature

by 5 or more: Th e target takes an additional 3 (1d6) Acid damage at

Aquatic Killer Th e wrakis can hold its breath for 30 minutes.
Cave Crawler Th e wrakis can climb diffi cult surfaces, including 
upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
Scurry Leap Th e wrakis can jump up to 20 ft. horizontally and 20

Encountering Infesting nearly every environment on the 
island, a Traveler is most likely going to chance upon the red 
insect in damp, dark environments. Th ere is little that garner 
this creature's attention more than a heap of scavenged offal 
to guard. While these remains would be a tasty meal for the 
arthropod, lying in wait to slay any other scavengers that would 
approach the potential meal, makes for an even fi ner catch.
With wide chitinous feet the creature can 
propel itself quickly through water, each 
of the four tarsi end in clawed tips to grip 
both bark and stone, allowing the beetle 
to climb most surfaces with ease 
A wide proboscis hosts a plethora of enzymes that 
can break down the interiors of both vertebrates 
and invertebrates, resulting in even bone to turn 
into a slurry of digestible pulp
Jittery Evasion (3/Day) Trigger: When an enemy the wrakis can 
see makes a ranged attack roll against it and before damage is 
dealt. Response: Th e wrakis can jump up to half its movement, 
potentially avoiding the attack by moving out of the line of sight 
or the attack’s range.

As the insect is a far ranging solitary hunter,

in a nearby crevice to later hatch
